messages:
ashley: Heads up — around 08:12 UTC I saw apiserver latency spike in eu-west-3 and a flurry of lease renewals. Several GPU attach requests timed out and we got autoscaler churn. anyone oncall?
raman: I'm here. Can you paste the apiserver logs or a short snippet?
ashley: quick tail from one apiserver pod:```"level"="warn" msg="apiserver: request took too long" path=/api/v1/... latency=3.2s code=503
E0320 08:12:34.123456 1 controller_manager.go:123] controller failed: lease renew failed: context deadline exceeded
etcd: leader changed from 10.0.4.2 to 10.0.6.7 at 08:12:36```
claire: saw a concurrent alert: conntrack saturation on the NAT gateway cluster in eu-west-3. WireGuard mesh rollout finished last night; might be flooding conntrack because of heavy GPU attach websocket traffic.
vince: yep — the WireGuard peer counts jumped to ~330k connections on gw-az1 at 08:11. conntrack table default is 65536, we hit TIME_WAIT/ESTAB exhaustion.
raman: that explains the controlplane retries -> leader jitter -> controller-manager timeouts -> attach delays. conntrack drops packets which makes kubelet healthcheck RTT spike and apiserver request fanout stall.
ashley: quick check command I ran on the NAT box: ```sudo conntrack -L | wc -l # -> 65789```
claire: also saw kube-proxy logs showing `failed to create conntrack entry: table full` on a few nodes.
vince: short mitigation — increasing nf_conntrack_max on the NAT boxes helps immediately. I'm pushing a canary to the three gateways in eu-west-3: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`
raman: can we also temporarily disable the WireGuard mesh on the gateway pool to see if attach success rate recovers?
vince: I can toggle one gateway to legacy routing (no mesh) to compare. doing it on gw-az1 now.
sre-bot: [alert] apiserver 5xx rate increased to 12% in eu-west-3 at 08:13:02 — source: prometheus/alerts
ashley: after raising conntrack on gw-az1 attach failures dropped from ~18/min to ~2/min. but autoscaler already killed some spot GPU instances.
claire: cost note: we had allowed burst to preemptible GPUs to save $$; that made recovery worse because nodes terminated and reattachment retried. When controlplane slows, preemptible churn amplifies.
raman: for medium-term we should: 1) tighten conntrack/keepalive defaults for WireGuard peers, 2) add NAT gateway autoscaling and conntrack provisioning in the controlplane runbook, 3) avoid preemptibles below a threshold when controlplane RTT > 200ms.
vince: I'll open a PR for a runbook patch and a rollout guard that prevents burst preemptible scale-ins when controlplane SLO unhealthy.
ashley: immediate ops: vince rolled sysctl on gw-az1-3, wireguard toggled on gw-az1 off. apiserver 5xx dropped to 1.1% in 3m, attach lat p50 -> 120ms p95 -> 540ms.
claire: logging note — captured a pcap and a short conntrack dump, uploading to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/eu-west-3/1729456789/conntrack.pcap
raman: good. when we stabilise we should reconcile the etcd leader churn timeline with the mesh rollout change. also annotate the GPU billing spike: we still paid for failed attach timeouts and spot reboots.
vince: I'll add the cost tally to the incident doc and flag on infra-costs. Shortterm PR: add conntrack autoscale + sysctl template + rollout gating.
ashley: TL;DR: WireGuard rollout + NAT conntrack defaults caused controlplane request drops -> leader jitter -> controller-manager lease retries -> GPU attach failures and preemptible churn. Mitigated by increasing conntrack max and toggling mesh on a gateway. Next steps in the runbook PR. :thumbsup:
